title: Three representative directions
reading: The slide organizes computer vision tasks into three directions defined by the flow between semantics (the word "tree"), the image/video, and the underlying 3D/4D scene. Recognition maps images to labels, generation maps labels/text to images, and reconstruction maps images to scene geometry. A red caption notes that language can enter at any stage. A pinhole-camera figure credited to Torralba, Isola, and Freeman anchors the image-to-scene relationship.

visuals.description: Left: the word "tree" with a yellow leftward arrow labeled "1: Recognition" and a rightward arrow labeled "3: Generation" pointing toward an image; below, a rightward arrow "2: Reconstruction" pointing from image/video to 3D/4D scene. Center-right: pinhole camera schematic with a tree scene projecting through a pinhole in a black plane onto a wall/projection surface, with green and brown rays crossing and forming an inverted image.
visuals.assertion: Vision tasks are directional mappings among labels/language, images/video, and the 3D/4D scene; imaging itself is a pinhole projection from scene to image.

concepts.name: Pinhole camera projection
concepts.why_it_matters: Explains how a 3D scene forms a 2D image.

verbatim_spans: Language can play in the middle of any stages!
[Figure credit: A. Torralba, P. Isola, and W. T. Freeman, Foundations of Computer Vision.]
